summary: Showed the pointer on the portable path and PROVED it in the artifact; built the driver half on the VS Code path and proved that too; and then found, by measurement, that the VS Code recording still cannot show a cursor for a reason the standing diagnosis had explicitly ruled out. WEB PATH, DONE: a synthetic pointer is drawn into the page and walked to each target -- the only mechanism available there, because Chromium's recordVideo composites no system cursor at all. check-pointer-visible.js crops the recorded frames at the instant before the pointer set off and the instant it arrived: 6 of 6 probes show a compact, cursor-shaped mark 18-20 x 27-31px with its tip within 2px of the click point, while a control recorded with identical timing and an identical probe list reads 0.00000 at every target. The first version of that check PASSED the control, because both sampled frames straddled the emphasis fade and the typing; fixed by holding the page still around both instants and by deriving the ~200ms gap between the run's clock and the video's own zero. The pointer also survives a native modal (9.0% visible over a full-bleed dialog against exactly 0 without the fix), because the browser's top layer beats any z-index and the pointer must be RE-promoted each time or a later-opened dialog covers it. VS CODE PATH, DRIVER DONE: the real Windows pointer is walked to each target, calibrated against the window by measurement rather than DPI arithmetic (three probe points, solved from two, checked against the third; residual 0px). Opt-in, announced before it takes the mouse, and restored on every exit path including failure. Three silent failures found on the way: the PowerShell driver read its own script from the stdin it needed for move commands; its type compilation was still running when the first moves were sent; and real pointer motion reaches only the window that is IN FRONT, which needs always-on-top because Windows refuses SetForegroundWindow to a background process. VS CODE PATH, CAPTURE BROKEN: with the driver working the frames still had no cursor, so the premise was measured instead of repeated. Three backends, two instruments: OBS window capture on WGC puts the workbench in frame (0.9996) and NO cursor (0.00000); OBS BitBlt draws the cursor onto a black frame, because it cannot read a hardware-accelerated Electron surface; only ffmpeg gdigrab over the window's desktop rectangle produces both (0.9697 / 0.124). Session 4's gdigrab probe is not contradicted -- it measured gdigrab title=<window>, a different mode with the same black-frame failure. No backend was swapped: none of the S4 pilot's seven criteria has been run against gdigrab, and the recorder is gated closed pending an operator ruling regardless. ALSO SHIPPED: ai_router.speed_ramp, which derives which stretches of a recording were waiting from the framework's own timestamps AND from movement sampled out of the recording itself -- the record is authoritative and sparse, so a person reading the screen otherwise looks exactly like a suite running. Marks are never compressed, so the two sources can only add real-time segments, never remove one. Proved on this set's own session 6 (2h58m of record, 29 marks, plans to 6m08s) and applied end to end to a real video (predicted 22.46s, produced 22.52s). Plus the publication safety checklist and the single-module tutorial's toy project, session-set plan and runbook. VERIFICATION: four rounds, $2.80, gpt-5-6-sol with anthropic excluded. It caught a REGRESSION I had introduced in this same session -- having measured that BitBlt is the only OBS method whose cursor setting does anything, I wired the physical pointer to select it, trading a video with no pointer for one with no product -- and then caught two more real defects in the fixes, including that the top-layer measurement had the same blind spot as the code it was validating. Closed WAIVED at the enforced bound on operator adjudication: five Majors remain, none disputed, all recorded as residuals with owners. Suites after the last code change: pytest 5091 passed, mocha 1580 passing, playwright 37 passed.

residuals.summary: No long-form human-driven capture harness was built (the capture half of spec step 3). Blocked on the same backend.
The single-module tutorial has no recordings, no ramp plans and no per-video safety records. The written walkthrough stands alone (spec decision 4); the six videos are owed.

The pointer visibility check matches a bounding-box PROFILE -- small, compact, taller than wide, tip at the hotspot -- not the cursor's pixels. Accepted: the same instrument must take a cursor this repo draws and a real Windows arrow in the operator's own theme and size. It demonstrably rules out the control at 0.00000, a full-width repaint, the hover tooltip that actually occurred at 6.5%, and a compact hover state.

The speed ramp cannot see a person reading a STATIC screen for longer than its 45-second threshold; fixing it properly needs input events, which nothing here captures. The opposite error is safe by construction -- an animated wait registers as movement and stays at real speed -- and the plan is a file that states the fraction it is compressing.
